subject: Eurasian jay
title: This Bird Planted Oak Forests Because It Forgets Its Snacks

scenes.text: One bird plants forests, and only because it forgets.
In autumn, a Eurasian jay buries acorns. Over a thousand of them, every year.
It carries them one at a time, sometimes as far as twenty kilometers from the oak.
It returns to eat many through winter. But a few acorns never get found.
Each forgotten acorn sits in soil, far from its parent tree, ready to sprout.
Jays helped oaks spread north after the last ice age. A forest, planted by lost snacks.

description:
The Eurasian jay buries over a thousand acorns a year and forgets some of them.
Those forgotten acorns grow into oaks, and jays helped oak forests spread north after the last ice age.
What would you plant if you could never remember where? Tell us below.
first_comment: Jays plant oaks by accident. What other animal helps nature without trying?
